transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Yeah, um, thanks. So, what brings me in... honestly, it’s work stuff. I work in video production, mostly camera operating and editing. I’ve been doing it forever, since I got my bachelor's. I actually wanted to do documentaries originally, like wildlife stuff? I went to Costa Rica once for a student film and it was incredible, the tree frogs there are so loud at night, though the humidity completely ruined one of my favorite lenses... but anyway, I do a lot of corporate and commercial stuff now. 

But what finally scared me into actually coming in here is that I just keep making these really dumb technical mistakes. Like, mistakes I absolutely know better than to make. I'll label the camera cards wrong on set, or I'll totally miss a timecode note from the producer. The other day, I exported a final client cut with the wrong lower-third graphic on the screen, and that was even after I specifically checked it. I swear I looked right at it! 

It was for this big tech startup, they make these smart-collars for dogs that track their vitals. Really cute dogs on that shoot, actually. There was this one golden retriever who kept trying to eat the boom mic, which is a nightmare for audio but hilarious to watch... but yeah, wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, why I'm here. Yeah, the mistakes. It's just getting really embarrassing and I don't know why I keep doing it.
Can you tell me more about how these mistakes happen? Do you find yourself having trouble focusing or feeling distracted when you're working?

I mean... I don't really think I'm distracted? Like, I'm not sitting there daydreaming or looking out the window. I feel like I'm staring right at the monitors. I have this dual-monitor setup at my desk, plus a calibrated reference monitor. I mostly cut in Premiere Pro, though honestly a lot of people in the industry are pushing me to switch to DaVinci Resolve. Resolve is incredible for color grading, actually. 

I tried to teach myself how to use it a few months ago because I had this gig shooting a promo for a local chef, and the kitchen lighting was this horrible mixed color temperature. Like, he had these super warm tungsten bulbs overhead, but bright blue daylight was just pouring in through the windows. It is a total nightmare to fix in post when you have mixed lighting like that. I spent hours tweaking the greens because the basil on his pasta looked literally neon... 

But, um... wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, focusing. Yeah, I don't know, I'm not sure if it's a focus thing. I feel like I'm paying attention, but then I'll just click the wrong thing or skip a step and I don't even realize I did it until the client flags it.
Have you been having any persistent, unwanted thoughts or finding yourself needing to do certain things over and over to feel like they’re just right?

No, I don't think so. Like, I don't have to tap the desk three times before I hit export or anything like that. Though honestly, with how buggy some of the software updates have been lately, I feel like I *should* start praying to the render gods or doing some kind of ritual. 

Adobe pushed this update last month that completely broke my dynamic link between Premiere and After Effects. I was working on this title sequence for a corporate training video—which, by the way, was the driest material I've ever had to sit through. It was all about compliance regulations for shipping hazardous materials. Did you know there are like, fifty different classifications just for batteries? Lithium-ion is a huge deal. You have to pack them a very specific way or they can literally catch fire on the plane. I actually watched a bunch of YouTube videos about battery fires after I finished that edit, and it is terrifying how fast they go up. 

But yeah, anyway, the software update... it just kept crashing my whole system. I had to roll back to the previous version, which is always a huge pain because then you have to worry about project file compatibility. But no, to answer your question, I don't have any weird, like, repetitive habits or unwanted thoughts. Just the normal amount of stress about my computer freezing.
Have you been feeling down, losing interest in things you usually enjoy, or feeling more tired than usual lately?

Down? No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I still love what I do, even with the technical screw-ups. I actually just bought a new drone last week—a DJI Mavic 3, the one with the dual-camera system. It's incredible. I took it out to the reservoir over the weekend to test the Hasselblad lens on it. The color science is just beautiful right out of the box. I was flying it over the water, and the way the sun was hitting the ripples... I ended up staying out there for like three hours, just burning through all my batteries. 

Which, speaking of batteries, reminds me of that hazardous materials video again. But yeah, I was having a great time. I'm definitely not losing interest in things. And tired? Not really. Honestly, sometimes I have the opposite problem. Like, I'll get so hyper-focused on tweaking a color grade or messing with a sound mix that suddenly it's 3 AM and I'm not even sleepy. My husband hates it because I'll come to bed and my brain is still going a million miles an hour about whether I should have used a J-cut or an L-cut in this one transition... but yeah, no, I'm not feeling depressed or tired or anything like that.
Do you often find yourself making mistakes or missing details because your mind is moving faster than your actions, or do you sometimes act on impulse without fully thinking things through?

Impulse... yeah, I guess so. Like, I'll jump in with an answer before the director or a client has even finished asking their question. I just hear the first few words and my brain is like, "Got it, I know exactly what you want," and I start talking. But then halfway through my sentence, I realize I'm answering the complete wrong thing because I didn't actually let them finish. 

It happens on set all the time. Like, last month we were shooting this commercial for a local car dealership, and the director started saying something about the lighting on the hood of the car, and I immediately started adjusting the C-stand with the silk on it. But it turned out he actually wanted to talk about a reflection from a window across the street that was catching the lens. 

Oh man, reflections are the worst when you're shooting cars. It's basically a giant mirror on wheels. We had to break out this massive black solid just to flag off the glare. And the dealership owner was there, hovering behind the monitor the whole time, which I absolutely hate. Having the client on set just adds so much pressure, you know? They always want to see the shot before it's lit, and then they panic because it looks terrible. I always have to explain that we haven't even brought in the key light yet. 

But yeah, I do that a lot—the blurting thing. I just react too fast.
Do you find yourself acting impulsively or having trouble slowing down in other parts of your life, like in conversations or while driving, not just at work?

Yeah, definitely in conversations. I do it all the time. I'll catch myself just cutting right into other people's conversations, like if I overhear someone talking about a movie or a piece of gear, I'll just jump right in. Or even at work, I'll lean over an assistant editor's shoulder and just grab the mouse to fix something on their timeline before they've even asked for help. I know it comes off like I don't trust them, which isn't true, I just... I see the problem and I want to fix it right then. 

It's like when I was trying to teach my husband how to use the espresso machine we got for our anniversary. It's this beautiful Breville, stainless steel, has the built-in grinder and the steam wand. It's a whole process, right? You have to dial in the grind size depending on the roast of the beans. We usually get these medium roast beans from a local roaster down the street, they have these great chocolate and cherry notes. Anyway, he was trying to froth the milk, and he was holding the pitcher at the completely wrong angle, and the milk was just screaming. You know that horrible screeching sound it makes when you don't introduce enough air? I couldn't handle it. I just reached over and grabbed the pitcher out of his hand to fix the angle. He got so mad at me. He was like, "I'm never going to learn if you just do it for me!" And he's right, but the sound was just... I couldn't just stand there and let him ruin the microfoam. 

So yeah, I definitely have trouble slowing down and letting other people do things at their own pace.
